cases.name: NIH Case: Cardiomegaly
cases.impression: 1. Cardiomegaly with a cardiothoracic ratio of 0.53, consistent with the patient's known history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. 2. Clear lungs without overt signs of acute alveolar pulmonary edema or pleural effusion at this time.
cases.dictation_transcript: In this 68-year-old female admitted for progressive dyspnea and orthopnea in the setting of HFrEF, the frontal chest radiograph demonstrates borderline cardiomegaly with a cardiothoracic ratio of 0.53 and left heart prominence. The lung parenchyma remains clear without overt alveolar edema or pleural effusions. Clinical correlation with volume status and cardiac biomarkers is advised.
cases.recommendations: 1. Assess volume status, serum NT-proBNP, and cardiac enzymes per ACC/AHA guidelines. 2. Correlate with recent 2D echocardiography to evaluate ventricular function and ejection fraction.

cases.name: Clinical Case: Pulmonary Nodule & Mass
cases.impression:
1. Left mid-zone pulmonary nodule (71.6%) and mass-like opacity (62.6%) in a heavy smoker with hemoptysis and weight loss, highly suspicious for primary bronchogenic carcinoma.
2. Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates (57.9%), indeterminate for active infection versus inflammatory or neoplastic lymphangitic spread.
3. Cardiomegaly with a CTR of 0.559.
cases.dictation_transcript: This is a 64-year-old male with a significant smoking history presenting with weight loss and hemoptysis. Frontal chest radiograph demonstrates a left mid-zone pulmonary nodule and mass, accompanied by bilateral interstitial infiltrates and a cardiothoracic ratio of 0.559. Given the high clinical suspicion for malignancy in the setting of hemoptysis and weight loss, an immediate contrast-enhanced chest CT is recommended.
cases.recommendations:
1. Perform a dedicated contrast-enhanced thin-slice chest CT per Fleischner Society guidelines for accurate nodule and mass risk stratification.
2. Pulmonology and oncology consultation for possible diagnostic bronchoscopy or image-guided transthoracic needle biopsy.
3. Sputum cytology and infectious workup including sputum cultures and AFB smears.

cases.name: NIH Case: Thoracic Mass & Consolidation
cases.impression:
1. Left mid lung zone pulmonary nodule/mass (69.9% probability). Indeterminate etiology requiring further cross-sectional imaging correlation.
2. No acute cardiopulmonary decompensation or pleural effusion.
cases.dictation_transcript: This is a frontal chest radiograph for a 58-year-old female presenting with subacute chest discomfort and fevers. Deep learning models and Grad-CAM localization highlight a focal pulmonary nodule in the left mid lung zone with a confidence score of nearly seventy percent. The cardiothoracic ratio is normal at 0.38, and pleural spaces are clear. Given the localized opacity, urgent contrast-enhanced chest CT is recommended to rule out primary neoplasm or inflammatory etiology.
cases.recommendations:
1. Perform a dedicated contrast-enhanced thin-slice chest CT for nodule characterization per Fleischner Society 2017 guidelines.
2. Correlate with inflammatory markers and clinical symptom progression.

cases.name: Clinical Case: Atelectasis & Fibrosis
cases.ctr_status: Normal for AP Portable (<0.55; AP magnification adjusted)
cases.impression: 1. Mild right mid zone subsegmental atelectasis related to post-operative shallow breathing and underlying interstitial lung disease. 2. No acute focal consolidation, overt pulmonary edema, or pleural effusion.
cases.dictation_transcript: This is an AP portable chest radiograph for a 71-year-old male post-operative on the medical ward with mild hypoxemia. We observe mild subsegmental atelectasis in the right mid lung zone, supported by an automated probability score of 63.7 percent and Grad-CAM localization. The cardiothoracic ratio is 0.536, which is normal for an AP portable view. No acute airspace disease or pleural effusion is seen, and recommendations include aggressive incentive spirometry and pulmonary hygiene.
cases.recommendations: 1. Initiate aggressive incentive spirometry, deep breathing exercises, and early ambulation per post-operative pulmonary care guidelines (ATS/ACCP). 2. Serial clinical monitoring of oxygen saturation and respiratory status. 3. Follow-up chest radiograph if clinical status deteriorates or fails to improve.

cases.name: Clinical Case: Acute Pneumonia & Infiltration
cases.impression:
1. Pulmonary infiltration / early bronchopneumonia in the left mid lung zone (53.1% confidence).
2. Suboptimal projection chest radiograph with clinical correlation strongly recommended.
cases.dictation_transcript: This is a 72-year-old male presenting to the emergency department with high fever and productive cough. Frontal chest radiograph demonstrates subtle pulmonary infiltration localized to the left mid lung zone with a normal cardiothoracic ratio of 0.452. Given the clinical presentation of high fever and comorbidities, urgent initiation of guideline-directed antimicrobial therapy and close monitoring are warranted.
cases.recommendations:
1. Initiate guideline-directed antimicrobial therapy per ATS/IDSA recommendations immediately.
2. Recommend interval follow-up chest radiograph in 4 to 6 weeks to document complete radiographic resolution.
3. Monitor vital signs and oxygen saturation continuously in the Emergency Department.

cases.name: Normal Baseline Control
cases.impression: 1. Normal chest radiograph with no acute cardiopulmonary disease. 2. Fully cleared for preoperative assessment.
cases.dictation_transcript: This is a 45-year-old female presenting for routine preoperative cardiopulmonary clearance. The frontal chest radiograph demonstrates clear lung fields bilaterally with no focal consolidation or acute infiltrates. The cardiomediastinal contours are normal and pleural spaces are clear. There is no acute thoracic abnormality detected.
cases.recommendations: 1. Routine clinical follow-up as clinically indicated per ACC/AHA preoperative guidelines. 2. No urgent thoracic imaging or additional diagnostic workup required.
